chapter: A&M, Indian music and the California fusion attempt
title: Forgotten Fantasies, the duo record with Richie Beirach
summary: Snyder let him record a duo album at Electric Ladyland to capture his harmonic language with Beirach.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: You went from there to doing Forgotten Fantasies, which is a duo record.

I wanted to give me and Richie – right, and John said yes. We did it at Electric Ladyland, because me and Richie by then really had – it was the beginning of our – this harmonic thing we play, in the way we play. I want to get that on tape. He said sure. John was cool. Duo record, on a major label, trying to be commercial. I mean, look, he did the Revolutionary Ensemble. Come on. If you do the Revolutionary Ensemble with my friend Leroy Jenkins, I think you could do Dave Liebman and Richie playing Forgotten Fantasies. So it wasn’t a big leap for John, because he was just doing whatever he could. He was going crazy. They gave him a blank check. He did what he wanted to.
Yeah, he did. He got a lot done. He did.
